htn_kidney.abstract: Hypertensive nephropathy is the second contributing factor to end-stage renal disease, while the relationship between the difference between estimated glomerular filtration rates (eGFRdiff) and rapid kidney function decline (RKFD) in hypertensive patients remains unclear. This study included 2,230 hypertensive patients from the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (CHARLS, 2011-2015). Multivariable logistic regression and restrictive cubic spline analysis were used to evaluate the association between eGFRdiff and the risk of RKFD. portal_hypertension.abstract: MASLD affects roughly one-third of people with HIV (PWH), yet data on advanced hepatic outcomes are limited. We examined the association of HIV co-infection with hepatic outcomes in propensity score-matched adults with MASLD. Using the TriNetX US Collaborative Network (~114.6 million patients), we identified adults with MASLD stratified by HIV status, excluding viral hepatitis, alcohol-related and other chronic liver diseases. Patients were 1:1 propensity-matched on demographics, BMI, smoking, cardiometabolic comorbidities, laboratory values and medications, then followed for 5 years (Kaplan-Meier, Cox, competing-risk analyses). portal_hypertension.abstract: Ascites is a rare complication of anorexia nervosa (AN) and is typically associated with hypoalbuminemia. Its influence on eating behavior and on the evaluation of treatment response remains poorly characterized. A 30-year-old woman with AN presented with massive ascites despite a preserved serum albumin level, a presentation not previously reported in adults. Imaging, ascitic fluid analysis, and serological testing excluded cirrhosis, malignancy, infection, and autoimmune serositis. The fluid showed a high serum-ascites albumin gradient (SAAG, 2.1 g/dL) with preserved protein (3.1 g/dL) and normal lactate dehydrogenase. portal_hypertension.abstract: MASLD is the most prevalent chronic liver disease and a significant cause of liver-related morbidity and mortality. Portal hypertension may develop before advanced fibrosis, driven by vascular and metabolic alterations that concurrently affect systemic haemostasis and promote intrahepatic interactions between endothelial dysfunction, inflammation, and haemostatic pathways. Once cirrhosis is established, the rebalanced haemostatic state is largely independent of aetiology, with impaired fibrinolysis representing the principal MASLD-associated difference.
